name: welcome
text: Hello, enquirer! Welcome to the tour of the Tabernacle of Moses. I will be your guide, as you discover the sacred furnishings and the holy vessels. I hope you're as excited as I am! Raise your left hand to read your tablet. When you are ready, choose Tour to visit a furnishing, or press A to continue.

name: altar
text: This is the bronze altar, made of acacia wood covered with bronze, with horns at its corners. Israelites brought offerings here; Aaron's priestly family handled the blood and the altar service. For a burnt offering, the worshipper laid a hand on the animal, and the priests presented its blood and burned the offering. The fire was kept burning, and ashes were carried to a clean place outside the camp. You can see bronze ash pots, shovels, basins, forks and firepans. Read Exodus 27:1–8, Leviticus 1:3–9 and Leviticus 6:8–13. This tour does not reenact sacrifices.

name: laver
text: This is the bronze washing basin and its bronze stand, between the altar and the tent. They were made from the mirrors of women who served at the entrance. Aaron and his sons washed their hands and feet before entering the tent or serving at the altar. Exodus does not give the basin's measurements or exact shape. Read Exodus 30:17–21 and Exodus 38:8. Our clear water reflection lets you see your chosen avatar; that is an educational feature.

name: holy-place
text: This is the Holy Place, where priests served. The pure gold lampstand burned olive oil; Aaron tended its lamps. The bread table was acacia wood covered with gold. Twelve loaves were arranged before the LORD with frankincense, replaced each Sabbath, and the removed bread belonged to Aaron and his sons to eat in a holy place. The incense altar was also acacia wood covered with gold, with horns at its corners. Aaron burned fragrant incense morning and evening as he tended the lamps. Read Exodus 25:23–40, Exodus 30:1–9 and Leviticus 24:1–9. You can ask me about any of these furnishings.

name: veil
text: This veil separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place. It was made of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it. Their detailed appearance is not given, so our artwork is interpretive. Ordinary priestly service did not permit going beyond it whenever one wished. Leviticus 16 describes the high priest's prescribed preparation, incense and blood offerings for atonement. Read Exodus 26:31–33 and Leviticus 16:2–16. Choose Most Holy Place on your tablet to enter our educational view.

name: ark
text: This is the ark of the covenant: an acacia wood chest covered inside and outside with gold. It held the testimony given to Moses. Its cover was pure gold, with two cherubim spreading their wings above it; their faces turned toward the cover. The high priest entered this chamber under the prescribed conditions for atonement, bringing incense and sprinkling blood before and on the cover. Read Exodus 25:10–22 and Leviticus 16:11–16. Our visitor access is educational. Viewing assistance on your tablet can help you see higher without changing the ark's dimensions.
